scenes.text: How does Google Photos find your dog, when you just type the word dog? [1] And how does Spotify know which songs feel similar? [2] The answer is something called embeddings.

An embedding takes something, like a word, a sentence, or even an image, [1] and turns it into a list of numbers that captures its meaning. [2] So meaning becomes numbers, [3] and things with similar meaning end up close together. [4] Think of it like giving every idea its own location on a map.

data.definition: A list of numbers that captures the meaning of text, images or sound.

scenes.text: So picture a map of meaning. [1] Here, the fruits cluster together, the animals sit over here, and the vehicles are over there. [2] Now, let's search for puppy. [3] And its nearest neighbours are dog and cat. Not because the spelling matches, but because the meaning does.

data.heading: A map of meaning
data.note: Search by meaning, not by spelling

scenes.text: And this is called vector search. Here's how it works. [1] First, every document is turned into an embedding, [2] which is just a list of numbers, [3] and it's saved in a vector database. [4] When you search, your question is turned into numbers too, [5] and the database returns the closest matches, in milliseconds.

And trust me, you've already used this. [1] Google Photos finds beach photos, even without any tags. [2] Spotify and YouTube suggest songs that feel similar. [3] And online stores keep showing you, you may also like.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think search just matches exact keywords. [2] Not anymore. Embedding search matches meaning. So if you search for cheap flights, it can also find budget airfare, even with zero words in common.

data.fact: Embedding search matches meaning: “cheap flights” also finds “budget airfare”.

scenes.text: Quick quiz! In embedding space, which word sits closest to king? [1] Pause and think. <pause 3.2> [2] It's queen! They have similar meaning, so they sit close together. Comment queen if you got it!

Let's recap. [1] Embeddings turn meaning into numbers. [2] Things with similar meaning sit close together. [3] Vector databases search them by meaning, [4] and they power photo search, recommendations, and a lot more. [5] Next episode is the big one, RAG, and how to make AI answer from your own documents.
